question: Can we trust halal butchers when some are known to cheat?
answer:
Now, somebody is going to say that you didn't mention the fact that the majority (or many, I should say) of the halal butchers are actually cheating fraudsters. They're not sacrificing properly; they're purchasing from, you know, Walmart or whatever it is, Tyson's chicken or whatever it is, and then they make it halal.

We say: look, where you know this is happening, point that out, and make sure this brother or sister fears Allah. And you may expose this deviancy. If the person is pretending that it is zabihah and it's not, your job is to expose it. However, as the hadith of the Prophet ﷺ said: if the Muslim is saying it's halal, then unless you find out otherwise, you don't have to install spy cameras in his shop. You don't have to go monitoring where he gets it from. If it's something very clear, if it's something obvious (for example, you go to his shop, it's a halal shop, and behind the shop there are boxes of the haram chicken, right? And it's like, where did that come from? It's a halal shop), you can ask him, because now you're seeing something. You can ask him, "Brother, you have halal chicken inside and haram boxes outside?" Go ahead, no problem. But otherwise, it's not your job to go spying. You cannot do this; it's haram. When the Muslim says it is zabihah, you trust that Muslim, and if he is lying, he has to answer to Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. You've done your job.

So I am the first person to say: I agree with you. There's a lot of cheating going on in this business; I'm the first person to say this. And I personally am very hesitant to just walk into any shop, and I try my best. It's sad to say, and I know I'm going to get a lot of pushback for saying this (I don't know if I should say it or not), but I actually trust the efficiency of kosher more than I trust the efficiency of most halal shops. I'm sorry for saying this. I'm talking about the efficiency, not the politics. By efficiency, I mean that if it says kosher, I can pretty much be certain that the name of Allah was mentioned, and the strokes were done properly, and the blood gushed out, because there was a certified rabbi that was there. Whereas in many halal shops, I have no clue what is happening, and I don't know who's doing what.

And therefore I try my best, when I go to a community, to find out which of the brothers are known to be practicing, going to the masjid, because they fear Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala; then if they're going to advertise it as halal, you go to those shops. And there are people (well, let's be honest here) you never see in the masjid, ever, and they're the ones running some of the butcher shops. And that's something that is a bit strange, because if you're that conscious that you want to sell halal meat, you should be coming for Jumu'ah, right? So these are questions; I agree with you. Nobody's denying this. And we should try our best to find out and make sure that halal is being monitored.

And I am the first to say we should have a national halal body, just like our Jewish cousins. They have rabbis that certify the K that is on meat products, or whatever products, that it's kosher; it is federal law. If you have something stamped that is not kosher, you can potentially go to jail; you're breaking federal law. Can you imagine? They have the government behind them. We are more than them in terms of quantity in America; there are more observant Muslims than there are Orthodox Jews. Why can't we do the same? Why can't we also have halal stamping? Shouldn't we be lobbying for this and petitioning for this? Definitely something that I'm a big advocate of. So that's one thing.
